correctness.rationale: Exact t(P)=2i(P)-1+m(P) follows by separating pure and mixed finite one-point extensions. Removing a maximal point x yields i(P)=i(P\{x})+i(H), where H is induced on points incomparable to x; every h-point poset has at least h+1 ideals, proving i(P)>=n+1+j(P). Comparable a<b inject into admissible mixed types via (down(a),up(b)), so m(P)>=c(P). The two nonnegative slacks give the exact defect. A connected nonchain has a fork or cofork producing a nonprincipal mixed type; hence m=c iff disjoint union of chains. Product formula for ideals then gives defect 2 sum_{r>=3}e_r and equality iff at most two nonempty chain components. Empty case verified. Checker reproduces all 4474 labeled posets through five points; no finite enumeration is used as an all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed new statement is the sharp coefficient-one penalty t(P) >= binomial(n+2,2)+j(P), its globally exact two-chain equality classification, and the two-term structural defect. Dolinka–Masulovic give the lower/upper one-point-extension representation, while the inspected published #P-completeness work gives the basic exact counting problem; neither inspected work yields or states this uniform extremal penalty. Prior exact second-minimum claims restrict optimization by only poset size, not arbitrary incomparability count. value.rationale: The number of incomparable pairs is an intrinsic structural statistic: the theorem determines its sharp universal coefficient-one contribution to the minimum nonalgebraic type count, then classifies every equality case. The exact defect cleanly distinguishes cross-component combinatorics from nonchain branching. This applies uniformly to arbitrary finite posets, beyond chain and antichain endpoints and a size-only second-minimum. Sharp structural extremality, not complexity or code correctness alone, supplies the mathematical reason for the result.
